name: Kushites
place: Napata and Meroë on the middle Nile
desc: The kingdom of the black pharaohs, whose kings ruled Egypt for a century, whose queens, the kandakes, led armies against Rome, and whose city of Meroë smelted so much iron that its slag heaps still stand. They built more pyramids than Egypt.
source: The victory stela of Piye; Meroitic inscriptions (readable, but the language is still barely understood); excavations at Meroë, Naqa and Jebel Barkal

cautious: kept the iron furnace burning for three days and nights
belligerent: marched north with the queen against the soldiers of Rome
devout: sang to the lion god at his temple in the desert

inventions.name: Iron of Meroë
inventions.source: Meroë smelted iron on a large scale from about the 5th century BCE; heaps of slag still surround the city
inventions.desc: Furnaces fed with charcoal and bellows turn red stone into iron for axes and spears: +2 attack, woodcutting 15% faster.
inventions.hint: Needs Bronze Metallurgy and iron ore.

inventions.name: Meroitic Script
inventions.source: From about 200 BCE the Kushites wrote their own language in a cursive script of 23 signs; it can be read aloud but not yet fully understood
inventions.desc: An alphabet of their own instead of borrowed hieroglyphs: the tribe gathers more lore.

inventions.name: Hafir Reservoir
inventions.source: Great earthen basins dug in the Butana plain to catch the summer rains, like the Great Hafir at Musawwarat es-Sufra
inventions.desc: A great round basin dug to hold the rain through the dry months: farm plots yield 15% more.

inventions.name: Steep Pyramids
inventions.source: Over 200 small, steep-sided pyramids stand at Meroë, el-Kurru and Nuri, more than in all of Egypt
inventions.desc: Narrow, steep pyramids of sandstone over the tombs of kings and queens: rites bring 15% more devotion, +2 mood.
inventions.hint: Needs Polished Stone Tools and the Bronze & Mythic Era.

inventions.name: Cotton Cloth
inventions.source: Cotton was spun and woven at Meroë in the early centuries CE, among the earliest in Africa
inventions.desc: Soft white cloth spun from cotton bolls: the cold bites 10% less, +1 mood.

foods.name: Sorghum Beer
foods.desc: Thick sorghum beer brewed in great jars, food and drink at once: +3 mood.

foods.name: Dom Palm Bread
foods.desc: The hard fruit of the doum palm, ground into a sweet flour that keeps: food spoils 8% slower.

finds.name: Red Iron Stone
finds.desc: Heavy red-brown sandstone full of iron, for the furnaces.

finds.name: Wild Cotton
finds.desc: Bushes whose seed pods burst into white fluff.

people.name: Dekarkhe
people.desc: He can tell the heat of a furnace by the colour of its smoke.
memory: drew the first bloom of iron out of the furnace

people.name: Nawidi
people.desc: In Kush the chief's mother chooses the next chief, and she chooses carefully.
memory: chose the young chief from among four brothers

people.name: Piye
people.source: The Victory Stela of Piye, c. 728 BCE (Egyptian Museum, Cairo)
people.desc: The Kushite king who conquered Egypt and was angrier that a defeated prince had starved his horses than at anything else he did.

people.name: Alara
people.source: Remembered in later Kushite inscriptions as the first of the royal line
people.desc: The first king of Napata, who gave his sister to the god Amun so that her descendants would rule.

people.name: Celer
people.source: Seneca (Natural Questions 6.8) and Pliny record two centurions Nero sent up the Nile to find its source, about 61 CE
people.text: a soldier from the far north, looking for where the river begins, who says his king wants to know.
memory: followed the river south until the marshes swallowed it
people.desc: One of Nero's explorers; the game names him, since the sources do not.

people.name: Taharqa
people.label: Taharqa, Pharaoh of Two Lands
people.desc: A Kushite pharaoh who builds from Napata to Memphis. Crafting 7, Combat 6.

people.name: Amanirenas
people.label: Amanirenas, the One-Eyed Kandake
people.desc: A queen who fights Rome to a treaty. Combat 8.

people.name: Amanishakheto
people.label: Amanishakheto, Queen of Gold
people.desc: A kandake whose gold jewels fill museum cases. Trade 7, Lore 5.

events.title: The Head Under the Steps
events.source: In 24 BCE the Kushites sacked Roman Aswan; a bronze head of Augustus they carried off was found buried beneath the steps of a temple at Meroë in 1910
events.text: The war party has come back from the north with the bronze head of the enemy's ruler, torn from his statue.

options.label: Bury it under the temple steps

do.feat: Buried the enemy's head under the temple steps

options.result: Now everyone who climbs to the god treads on the enemy's face.

options.label: Send it back with an offer of peace
options.result: The enemy is surprised, and agrees to a treaty that asks no tribute.

events.title: The Starved Horses
events.source: Piye's stela: 'That my horses should be hungered pains me more than any crime you have done.' His horses were buried near his pyramid at el-Kurru
events.text: Men from a beaten village are brought in. In their stables the chief finds horses so thin their ribs show. The chief is furious.

options.label: Punish them, feed the horses
options.result: The horses are taken into the chief's own stables and fattened.

options.label: Forgive, and teach them
options.result: The herders are shown how to keep horses. Their village joins ours.

events.title: Smoke over the City
events.text: The furnaces burn day and night now. Black slag is piling up into hills around the village, and the acacia groves are being cut for charcoal.

tales.name: Apedemak the Lion God
tales.source: The Lion Temple at Naqa, 1st century CE
tales.text: Our god of war has the head of a lion. On the temple wall he is carved with three lion heads and four arms, and a snake's body rising from a lotus. He leads the queen's archers, and he lets the lions eat the enemies of Kush.

tales.name: The Table of the Sun
tales.text: In a meadow outside the city there is a table always covered with roasted meat. The magistrates fill it by night, and by day anyone who wishes may come and eat. The people say the earth itself gives it.

tales.name: Piye Goes North
tales.text: When the king heard that the princes of the north were at war, he sent his army with a command: purify yourselves in the river before battle, and fight by day, never by night like thieves. Then he went north himself, and every city opened its gates to him, and he gave thanks in the temple of Amun.

tales.name: How the Queen Mother Chooses
tales.source: A story made up around the role of the king's mother in Kushite succession
tales.text: When the old king dies, his brothers and sons stand before the queen mother. She does not ask who is strongest. She asks each of them to feed the hungry for a day, and watches. The one the people bless is the one she names.
tales.moral: a ruler is chosen by the people's blessing
